safetyAndScope.browser: Root uses T3 collaborative preview; this axis did not use standalone Playwright
safetyAndScope.reviewOwnership: This report owns state/API/database/router; private native/import/pixel/provider/pack/deployment review is independently owned by Spec. Every pending path is inventoried below.

standards.interpretation: Repository docs define behavioral/privacy/recovery boundaries, not separate coding-style rules. Formatting/types/tool-enforced issues were excluded. The findings below are concrete behavioral defects against those contracts. Fowler smell labels remain heuristic judgments, never hard violations.

judgmentCalls.originalHunk: Autosave effect, pagehide and persist each call writeDraft(owner, draft), while clear separately deletes the same IndexedDB owner record.
judgmentCalls.concreteHarm: Independent unconditional writes/deletes had no shared cross-tab version contract, allowing lost photos and stale discard.
judgmentCalls.resolution: CreatorDraftStorage serializes operations and performs compare-and-swap inside one IndexedDB readwrite transaction.

judgmentCalls.originalHunk: requestKey is a UUID string regenerated by every update; a characters row alone stores request_key.
judgmentCalls.concreteHarm: An unbound string did not distinguish an unsubmitted draft, an ambiguous paid submission, an accepted receipt or a deleted request; deletion/case variants could buy work again.
judgmentCalls.resolution: Persistent submitted marker and durable owner-scoped, case-insensitive creation receipts bind request identity to payload and deletion/cancellation state.

standards.notReported: Large existing UI/router modules and ordinary delegation/helpers were not flagged solely for size, style, speculative reuse or naming preference.

findings.title: A stale tab can submit one account's saved private photos to another account after the shared cookie changes
findings.reproduction: Tab A displays account A and its local draft/photo. Tab B changes the shared cookie to B. Original mine/create uses the new cookie while ownerRef still says A; response B is applied to A UI and A photo is billed/owned as B.
findings.redEvidence: HTTP expected-owner mine returned 200 instead of 409. Root independently reproduced in T3 browser: A still displayed, B-owned ready job custom_45397bfd6168426a93d5c4d58a593767 created from A draft; exactly one fixture design/draw, zero billing.
findings.fix: Updated browser sends X-Creator-Owner for every private operation and signout. Server rejects mismatch before parsing multipart. Typed 401/SESSION_CHANGED exits to login while preserving per-account local draft. Auth changes broadcast across tabs. Every auth event invalidates initial/signin response epochs, including while loading, so stale responses cannot reopen another account's IndexedDB draft. Stale action callbacks are guarded.
tests: a tab bound to one account cannot read, upload, or sign out the account selected by another tab
browser requests bind private operations to the displayed account and preserve typed session failures
findings.greenEvidence: HTTP/client regression green. Root T3 cross-tab logout immediately hides A draft on auth change. Delayed initial/signin callback browser verification is recorded by root separately.

findings.title: Deleting a character or changing UUID letter case defeats paid request deduplication
findings.reproduction: Create with key, wait for failed/ready, delete nonpublished character, resend same key. Or replay an accepted UUID using uppercase letters. Only character rows were checked and case compared literally.
findings.redEvidence: Deletion replay returned 202 instead of 410 and a second generation started; uppercase replay returned 202 instead of 200 and a second row started.
findings.fix: Separate durable creation_requests ledger survives character deletion/restart; UUIDs canonicalize to lowercase and receipt key collation is case-insensitive. Deleted/archived/cancelled receipts return 410. Receipt plus job plus attempt are written in the same existing budget transaction. Migration preserves legacy accepted keys.
tests: deleted creation keys remain tombstoned across restart and cannot reserve another paid attempt
UUID letter case cannot bypass accepted-request identity
legacy accepted keys migrate without another paid call and bind matching normalized photo content
findings.greenEvidence: All green; one attempt/draw retained across deletion/restart/case replay. Empty authenticated recovery and matching multipart recovery work with generation disabled.

findings.title: An accepted UUID silently returns an unrelated changed input/photo payload
findings.reproduction: Reuse an accepted key with a different name or photo. Original early lookup returns the old fighter before parsing multipart.
findings.redEvidence: Changed name replay returned 200 instead of conflict409.
findings.fix: Bind accepted request to canonical schema-parsed input and ordered photo-byte SHA-256 digests; mismatched multipart receives REQUEST_KEY_REUSED409. Empty authenticated POST remains a recovery query. Legacy rows compare canonical input and normalized stored photos before first hash binding, so matching old requests remain usable.
tests: a request key binds to the input and photo bytes, while bodyless recovery works with generation disabled
legacy accepted keys migrate without another paid call and bind matching normalized photo content
findings.greenEvidence: Changed text/photo rejected; same payload/bodyless replay returns original id without budget reservation or model request.

findings.title: A lost POST response leaves the UI submitting indefinitely and edits can replace the reconciliation key
findings.reproduction: Hold/drop the response after create acceptance; fetch had no deadline and input changes still generated fresh UUIDs, so saved form could stop matching the accepted job.
findings.redEvidence: Source had no request abort signal and fields were enabled throughout POST; root had independently exercised a lost acceptance acknowledgement.
findings.fix: Persist submitted marker before POST, freeze exact input/photo/key while ambiguous, bound requests to45s, and permit explicit same-key check. Safe discard first stores a cancellation receipt, fencing a late original upload before it can reserve budget. Already accepted jobs remain in Mis luchadores. A draft persisted before any network call can be discarded/retried safely, so pending state is not permanent.
tests: a lost creation response is bounded, aborted once and never automatically retried
draft fields, exact pending UUID and private photo bytes survive reopening and remain scoped by owner
discarding a pre-network or still-uploading request fences its late POST without spending a generation attempt
zero-cost cancellation receipts have bounded daily admission and existing receipts remain usable
findings.greenEvidence: Deterministic held-open real HTTP multipart upload cancelled before completion returns410 after body arrives; attempts0, draws0, no upload folder. Explicit pre-network discard also fences later POST. Client abort occurs once, no retry.

findings.title: Two tabs can overwrite photos or resurrect/delete a newer saved draft
findings.reproduction: Two tabs load the same owner draft. One saves new photos; the older tab autosaves or discards its stale copy. Original put/delete have no version precondition.
findings.redEvidence: Original storage functions unconditionally put/delete owner record, verified source path; root current-browser tests are separate from deterministic storage regressions.
findings.fix: Queued per-session storage operations with compare-and-swap write IDs inside IndexedDB transactions; stale operations reject DraftConflictError. UI offers explicit recovery. Pending autosaves cannot run after a later clear snapshot; pagehide reads the latest ref and preserves owner scope.
tests: a stale tab cannot overwrite or discard another tab's newer photo draft
autosaves and discard execute in order and cannot resurrect the discarded draft
an aborted storage write preserves the committed draft and does not poison subsequent saves
findings.greenEvidence: Stale put and delete reject without altering latest photo/key; explicit reload reconciles. Ordered autosaves plus discard leave no record; aborted write retains committed draft and later save succeeds.

findings.origin: corrupt-data hardening and independent follow-up of new CAS implementation
findings.title: Malformed IndexedDB photo/version metadata can throw or permanently conflict with its own structured clone
findings.reproduction: Stored photos contains null, or writeId/requestKey is object/array. New initial CAS implementation accepted nonprimitive writeId and compared cloned objects by identity, so subsequent save/clear could never recover.
findings.redEvidence: Independent reviewer reproduced malformed version token. New regression initially failed with corrupt:false and an apparently valid draft for object writeId.
findings.fix: Validate every photo and metadata token; mark corruption visibly. CAS token always uses a primitive valid UUID or stable reserved corrupt token, allowing explicit repair/discard while rejecting a legitimate concurrent tab write.
tests: corrupt photo records fail closed with a visible corruption result and can be explicitly replaced
nonprimitive corrupt metadata remains recoverable instead of conflicting with its own structured clone
findings.greenEvidence: Object/array writeId and nonstring object/array requestKey now load as corrupt and both clear/save repair; no self-conflict.

redRuns.failure: object writeId incorrectly loaded as corrupt:false

validation.productionBuild: npm run build passed (Vite1635 modules; existing large bundle warning)
validation.historicalSuiteObservation: One initial concurrent suite cleanup raised ENOTEMPTY after shutdown. Focused adversarial-v31 rerun12/12 and final creator86/86 passed. Spec owner reviewed noncooperative async filesystem completion after abort; no reproducible product-state corruption established. Two other initial failures were old already-loaded duplicate-pose fixture snapshots, resolved with geometrically distinct fixture poses.
validation.fullRepoAndBrowser: Final full repository suite, browser screenshots and deployment validation owned by root and recorded separately; this report does not claim a new live API/native generation.

compatibilityAndRemainingRisks: Native plan/credit usage and semantic likeness/pose quality remain subject to Spec review and manual visual checks. This axis made zero paid calls.
Generation remains single-process. No distributed queue/lock guarantee is claimed; documented limits and restart/manual continuation behavior remain in force.

New browser always supplies expected-owner header and paid creation key. Optional absent headers preserve old client/direct HTTP compatibility; obsolete frontend bundles should reload to gain new cross-tab binding.

IndexedDB eviction, user-cleared site data, unavailable/quota-limited browser storage or another device can lose unsubmitted local photo drafts. Storage failure is visible and prevents submission without a successful pending save.

Cancelled/deleted receipts are retained indefinitely to fence delayed requests; rolling cancellation limits bound new zero-cost receipts to4x configured global/per-owner attempts per24h. Backups/storage monitoring must include receipt ledger.
Accepted requests deleted before this migration have no remaining identity to reconstruct; durable replay protection applies to retained/migrated rows and new receipts.
Timeout/abort cannot prove provider billing status. Existing failed/interrupted jobs require an explicit owner continuation; no automatic paid retry was added.
Malformed local records are rejected visibly and can be deliberately replaced; no claim is made to reconstruct corrupt photo bytes.
